reference: Installed less 668 (GNU regular expressions), /usr/bin/less, invoked by system Bash with private relative fixture files and redirected stdout. Copying and missing-file behavior use its exact byte/status oracle; Bash type/help builtins provide the metadata contract oracle.
coverage: Redirected stdin passthrough of small binary data, including NUL, CRLF, and an unterminated final record, compared with GNU less.
Repeated redirected stdin invocations in one Bash process, compared with GNU less.
Multiple relative file operands in redirected-output mode, compared with GNU less, including any headers in the actual command output.
Bash builtin type metadata and the loadable's registered help synopsis/options and interactive-key documentation.
Empty named files, binary bytes spanning operand boundaries, and explicit stdin operands in redirected plain-output mode.
Missing operands in redirected plain-output mode: exact stdout diagnostics, zero status, continuation through later private files and same-shell recovery.
exclusions: Interactive paging, search, resize, terminal restoration, and option behavior tied to terminal geometry are deferred because this runner supplies no PTY driver.
No result here claims GNU less interactive compatibility or physical-terminal qualification.
Only redirected plain-output copying and file-open errors are qualified. Interactive error handling, terminal-dependent options and stream read/write error parity remain unqualified.

cases.purpose: Compare nonterminal stdin copying byte for byte, including an embedded NUL, CRLF, and a final line without newline, against GNU less.
Ensure two less invocations reading different redirected files in the same Bash process each consume their own complete input, compared with GNU less.
cases.script: printf 'first input\n' > first; printf 'second input\n' > second; less < first; less < second

cases.purpose: Compare redirected output for two named relative files with GNU less; this checks whether less emits file-separator headers in its nonterminal drain path.
cases.script: printf 'first file\n' > first; printf 'second file\n' > second; less first second

cases.purpose: The compiled loadable is registered as a Bash builtin; type -t is Bash's metadata interface and should identify it as builtin.
Bash help metadata should document the source-declared synopsis and the supported -F, -N, -S, and -n options.
cases.script: doc=$(help less); [[ $doc == *"less [-F] [-N] [-S] [-n LINES] [FILE...]"* ]] || exit 1; [[ $doc == *"quit if content fits on one screen"* ]] || exit 1; [[ $doc == *"show line numbers"* ]] || exit 1; [[ $doc == *"chop long lines to screen width"* ]] || exit 1; [[ $doc == *"override screen-page size"* ]] || exit 1; printf 'synopsis and options documented\n'

cases.purpose: Bash help metadata should list the documented navigation/search keys and the no-controlling-terminal drain behavior.
cases.script: doc=$(help less); [[ $doc == *"space/f next page, b previous page"* ]] || exit 1; [[ $doc == *"g/G top/bottom"* ]] || exit 1; [[ $doc == *"/ and ? search, n/N repeat search"* ]] || exit 1; [[ $doc == *"When /dev/tty is unavailable, drains input without pausing."* ]] || exit 1; printf 'navigation and tty fallback documented\n'

cases.purpose: Exercise initial screen rendering, next/previous page and line movement, top/bottom navigation, and clean quit on a controlling terminal.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable VM or PTY-capable fixture driver with a controlling 24x80 terminal, deterministic multi-page input, scripted space/b/j/k/g/G/q keystrokes, captured screen/prompt bytes, and checks that termios and SIGWINCH state are restored.

cases.purpose: Exercise forward and reverse literal searches, repeat with n/N, and search input editing on a controlling terminal.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable VM or PTY driver to feed deterministic / and ? prompts, backspace edits, n/N repeats, and q; capture the visible matched lines and verify prompt cleanup.

cases.purpose: Exercise -F, -N, -S, and -n against known terminal dimensions and verify behavior when the terminal changes size.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable VM or controllable PTY with fixed and resized winsize values, short and long fixture lines, input just below/above the page size, and captured output checks for auto-quit, numbering, chopping, page count, and redraw.

cases.purpose: Empty files add no separators or bytes, and binary payloads concatenate exactly across file boundaries with no final newline inserted.
cases.script:
printf 'A\000B' > first
: > empty
printf '\r\nC' > last
less empty first empty last empty

cases.purpose: Check an empty named file produces no output and a dash operand reads a private redirected stdin stream in operand order.
cases.script:
printf A > first
printf 'B\000C' > standard-input
printf D > last
: > empty
less empty
less first - last < standard-input

cases.purpose: Compare exact redirected stdout diagnostics, zero status and operand-order continuation for missing files in first, middle and sole positions, then confirm a later same-shell invocation still copies normally.
cases.script:
printf A > first
printf 'B\n' > last
for operands in 'absent first last' 'first absent last' 'absent'; do
 rc=0; less $operands || rc=$?
 printf 'missing-status=%s\n' "$rc"
done
less last
